Implementation Details. For the Entity Perceiver (EP), we use a pre-trained GIT model and for Knowledge Extractor (KE), we use PaLM-2-L-IT LLM(Anil et al., 2023). Training Details. We train GIT, BLIP-2 and VIT-T5 for 42, 40 and 30 epochs respectively, using a batch size of 128, a learning rate of 1e-5, adamW (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2017) optimizer and cosine scheduler with a linear warmup. Metrics. We use the standard BLEU-4 (B-4), Rouge-L (R-L) and CIDEr metrics used in captioning tasks (Vedantam et al., 2015; Lin, 2004; Papineni et al., 2002). We also calculate an Entity $\mathrm{F_1}$ (Ent. $\mathrm{F_1}$ ) score to measure how well the ground-truth entities are covered in the generated caption, similar to (Liu et al., 2021; Bertsch et al., 2023). To this end, named-entities are extracted from ground-truth caption and generated caption, and then compared using $\mathrm{F_1}$ score. Among all metrics, we emphasize CIDEr and Ent $\mathrm{F_1}$ the most. CIDEr is important for evaluating caption quality as it strikes a balance between precision focused B-4 and recall focused R-L. On the other hand, Ent $\mathrm{F_1}$ is crucial for evaluating entities presence in the captions. Table 4: Ablation study on GIT to study the impact of our design choices.
